newsitem.title: USA: Simpson case cop pleads "no contest" to perjury.
newsitem.headline: Simpson case cop pleads "no contest" to perjury.

text.p: Ex-detective Mark Fuhrman was sentenced to three years' probation on Wednesday after pleading "no contest" to a charge he lied on the stand at the O.J. Simpson murder trial by testifying he never used a racial slur in the past decade.

Hours after first declaring his innocence, Fuhrman -- a key investigator in the murders of Simpson's ex-wife and her friend -- changed his plea to the perjury charge in a deal with prosecutors under which he avoided jail time.

If convicted on the felony perjury charge, Fuhrman could have been sentenced to three or four years behind bars. The charge stemmed from his denial on the stand last year that he had ever called black people "niggers."
Before approving the plea bargain, Superior Court Judge John Ouderkirk told the former Los Angeles police detective that the no contest plea amounted to an admission of guilt under California law.

Fuhrman's attorney, Darryl Mounger, told the judge he had opposed his client's decision, but noted that "he believes it's in his best interest to enter this plea" both for himself and for the people of Los Angeles.
The criminal case against Fuhrman, who retired in late 1995 and now lives in Idaho, stemmed from an 11-month investigation by the California attorney general's office.

The perjury charge was filed one year after a mostly black jury acquitted Simpson, a former football star and actor, in the killings of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman. The jury deliberated for less than three hours.

Fuhrman was accused of lying on the witness stand on March 15, 1995, when he testified that "he had not addressed any black person as a 'nigger' or spoken about black people as 'niggers' in the past 10 years," according to a criminal complaint.
Following his testimony, an aspiring screenwriter came forward with taped interviews with Fuhrman in which he uttered the racial slur dozens of times and bragged about beating and torturing suspects.

When Fuhrman was called back to the witness stand, he invoked his constitutional right against self-incrimination and refused to answer questions. The defence built its case around claims that Fuhrman was a racist who planted a bloody glove found at the black celebrity's estate after the murders.

California Attorney General Dan Lungren later defended the plea bargain, stressing that even though Fuhrman was not brought to trial, "the man is a felon. He's thoroughly disgraced and he stands before the world as a convicted liar."
Lungren told a news conference that such perjury cases were extremely rare and even if the prosecution had won a conviction, "no judge or jury would have jailed him."

Black leaders were disappointed with the outcome. "Mark Fuhrman should be behind bars, he should have been nailed to the wall," commented John Mack, president of the Los Angeles branch of the Urban League.

He praised the fact that a perjury charge was filed, "but I am unhappy the state cut a deal. At least it's formal recognition that he lied on the stand, but he walked away with a slap on the wrist," said Mack.

Fuhrman was arraigned on Wednesday in front of two different judges -- Municipal and Superior Court -- entering "not guilty" pleas both times. After waiving his right to a jury trial, he appeared at a third hearing within two hours and his attorney, Mounger, and prosecutor John Gordnier told Judge Ouderkirk they had agreed to settle the case.
Ouderkirk reviewed the agreement, then reconvened after lunch to announce his approval. Along with the three years' probation, Fuhrman was ordered to pay a $200 fine.

Prosecutors in Simpson's criminal trial had maintained that even though Fuhrman had clearly lied about his use of racial slurs, there was nothing to support claims that he tried to frame Simpson for the murders.
At one point on Wednesday, a man approached him in the courthouse hallway, shoved court papers toward Fuhrman and declared loudly: "You are served, buddy."

It was a subpoena from Simpson's attorneys ordering him to testify in the civil wrongful death case brought by the victims' families. Jury selection is now under way for Simpson's civil trial in Santa Monica.
